extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners before the USPTO; OED staff and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24: suspends respondent from practicing trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO, describes the factual/procedural bases for the discipline, conditions for reinstatement, and publication/notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to a suspension imposed by a duly constituted state authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent is given an opportunity to file a response within forty (40) days opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If no response is filed, there may be no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) grounds suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension from practice before the USPTO may be predicated upon being suspended for the same period from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order suspends Respondent for sixteen (16) months for violating § 11.804(h) predicated upon the Tennessee suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to Notice and Order creates no genuine issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response to the Notice and Order within the provided period, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter, the Notice and Order was delivered on July 2, 2022; Respondent did not file a response, and the Director determined reciprocal suspension appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impose suspension identical in duration to state discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline imposed by the USPTO should be the same duration as the discipline imposed by the state authority (here: sixteen (16) months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly suspends Respondent for sixteen (16) months, 'commencing on the date of this Final Order,' mirroring the Tennessee order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice until reinstatement petition granted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain excluded from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is a discretionary process governed by § 11.60 and may include conditions precedent (e.g., restitution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition precedent to reinstatement: restitution and reimbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition precedent to reinstatement, Respondent is required to make restitution to identified victims and reimburse the Tennessee Lawyer's Fund for Client Protection (TLFCP) if the TLFCP makes restitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific amounts in this order: restitution to Barbara Payne in the amount of $660.00 and to Tequia Williams in the amount of $4,524.51; if TLFCP pays restitution, Respondent must reimburse TLFCP the same amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access URL provided: http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov (or https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/ for disciplinary decisions). Publication is part of making the discipline available for public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette with materially consistent language
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the order's notice text describing the suspension and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order supplies model notice language summarizing the respondent's suspension, the basis (violations of Rules 1.3, 1.4, and 8.1), the scope (trademark/non-patent practice), and reference to the statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32; 37 C.F.R. § 11.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural requirement under § 11.59 to inform relevant authorities and the public about the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1.3 (diligence) violation: failing to make timely filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged violating Tennessee Rule of Professional Conduct 1.3 for failing to be diligent in making timely filings for patent and trademark matters for which he was retained, resulting in denial of those applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of diligence in filing and prosecution that results in denials is a substantive basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to perfect appeals of denials
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged failing to perfect appeals of denials of patent and trademark applications for which he had been retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pursue appeals of adverse substantive actions is cited as a distinct act contributing to discipline (tied to professional obligations to clients).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1.4 (communication) violation: failing to reasonably communicate with client
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged violating Tennessee Rule of Professional Conduct 1.4 by failing to reasonably communicate with his client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to keep clients reasonably informed and to respond to client inquiries supports discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8.1 (bar admissions and disciplinary matters) violation: failing to respond to Board inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged violating Tennessee Rule of Professional Conduct 8.1 by failing to respond to inquiries from the Board of Professional Responsibility of the Supreme Court of Tennessee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-cooperation with disciplinary authorities and failure to respond to inquiries constitutes misconduct supporting reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority citation: action pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The disciplinary action is taken pursuant to the statutory and regulatory authority of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders should cite appropriate statutory/regulatory authority when imposing discipline; these citations establish jurisdiction and basis for the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope statement in notice: clarify patent practice authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice should state the scope of the respondent's authorization before the USPTO (e.g., that the respondent is authorized to practice in trademark and non-patent matters and is not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice example in the order explicitly informs the public whether the respondent is authorized to practice patent matters before the USPTO.
